thesis: The book already pays you to believe in midterm autumn equity weakness: the event sleeve shorts SPY in midterm years on T2, and the seasonal work treats midterm as a de-risk conditioner. Nothing in it holds the cross-asset partner of that view. If midterm policy uncertainty pulls equities down into the autumn, the reserve currency is where that money sits, and August is thin enough that positioning moves price. The market prices this jobs print as a rates event and trades it through the front end. The variant perception is that in a midterm August the dollar is the cleaner expression, because the flow is a positioning unwind rather than a repricing of the path. title: Own the Nasdaq against the index for the inflation print, and nothing else

thesis: The market treats a CPI print as a direction event and hedges it with index exposure, which is why every vol-crush cell around this print has been arbitraged flat and why one died in this morning's checks. What is left is a dispersion effect nobody is positioned for. Across the 311 CPI eves since 2000 the Nasdaq has beaten the S&P by 11.5 basis points over the print session alone once the pair is hedged for beta, winning 59.8% of the time and in 22 of 27 calendar years. The other side is index-level hedging demand: desks manage event risk in the most liquid instrument they have, which pushes the broad index around on the print session while the rate-sensitive half of the tape reprices on the number itself, and a beta-matched pair collects the gap without taking a side on the number. The tell that this is structural rather than a momentum artifact is the direction split, because the equal-dollar version of the same spread makes its money only when SPY rallies and loses when SPY falls, while the beta-matched version does its best work on down sessions.

evidence.summary: Long QQQ against a beta-matched short SPY, sized at 1.48 dollars of SPY per dollar of QQQ from the point-in-time 126-day beta, entered MOC on the session before a CPI release and exited MOC on the print session. N=311 eves 2000-2026: mean +0.115% of the QQQ leg, hit 59.8%, t 2.76, sign p 0.00032, bootstrap P(mean<=0) 0.0036, and +0.108pp of excess over the spread's own all-days drift. The anchor is specific to CPI, since the identical construction pays -0.002% on PPI eves, -0.041% on NFP eves, +0.065% on FOMC eves and +0.007% on all days. It replicates on the underlying price indices with no ETF involved (^NDX against ^GSPC, +0.097%, 60.5% hit, sign p 0.00014) and survives every hedge definition tested, spanning +0.099% to +0.127% across 63, 126 and 252-day betas and two volatility-ratio hedges. Edge is 11.5 bps against a pair round trip of roughly 1 to 2 bps in the two most liquid ETFs listed, so this is a reliability trade rather than a size trade: at 30 bps the position is 20.5% of NAV gross, net market exposure is 0.02% of NAV, and the worst session in 26 years would have cost 0.22% of NAV. Computed fresh this morning against the 2026-08-10 close.
evidence.control: the spread's own all-days drift of +0.007% over the same one-session horizon; three placebo event anchors (PPI eve -0.002%, NFP eve -0.041%, FOMC eve +0.065%); and the equal-dollar construction of the same pair, which pays +0.085% and is the version that fails
evidence.era_note: Positive in 22 of 27 calendar years, sign test on years p 0.0008. Dropping the three best years still leaves +0.065% at sign p 0.0009. title: Own the long end from tonight's inflation close into tomorrow's producer print

exit.event_anchor: exit on the close of the PPI print session itself, 2026-08-13

orders.Place_Note: MOC parent with a time exit only

thesis: Tonight's close carries a risk premium for two inflation prints, not one. When CPI and PPI land on consecutive sessions the market prices the pair as a single block, and the duration holder gets paid to sit through the second, lower-information half of it: the PPI session pays TLT +25.8 bps when a CPI printed on its eve against +8.4 bps when one did not, and the session immediately before the print pays nothing at all. The other side is whoever bought protection across the block and unwinds it once the headline number is out, plus the rates shorts positioned for a producer print that almost never moves the story after CPI has. Consensus treats PPI as a footnote, which is the reason the premium survives to be collected. 95% of the payoff arrives in the 08:30 gap, so this is a one-session release trade and nothing else.

evidence.summary: PPI print session whose eve carried a CPI print, long TLT close to close: +25.8 bps raw, +22.2 bps against a trading-day-of-month matched control, record 35-20 (63.6% hit) against TLT's 52.1% unconditional base rate, bootstrap P(mean<=0) 0.034. The same print session without a CPI on its eve pays +5.6 bps excess at 55.5%, and the offset ladder is a one-session spike rather than a plateau (k=-1 -10.6 bps, the trade +25.8 bps, k=+1 -5.7 bps). Charged in full for the August month effect the honest expectation is +16.0 bps against a 2.6 bps all-in round trip, roughly 6x cost. 8 of 11 years positive with no single year carrying it (best 2025 +0.884% on N=5, 2020 +0.618% on N=7).
evidence.control: trading-day-of-month matched TLT drift, because a rates event cell measured against an all-days control is invalid: TLT's own unconditional return swings from -0.202% at tdom 2 to +0.215% at tdom 14 with no event anywhere. Cross-checked against a month x tdom double control, which reads +24.7 bps at a 69.1% hit.
evidence.era_note: 52 of 55 observations are 2018 or later, and that is by construction rather than a selected era: back-to-back CPI-then-PPI scheduling is a modern BLS calendar artifact. The cell therefore has one regime and can never have a second, which is why it is graded B and not A.

The edge is 95% overnight (+24.4 of +25.8 bps) and the damage is not: the worst session in the cell, 2022-08-11, gapped only -0.21% and closed -2.33%, and three of the five worst losses did more harm after the open than at it. A green gap fully retraced by 11:00 ET means the premium already released and the session has turned into a rates repricing this trade has no edge in.

The live long-GDX pitch running to 08-17 correlates +0.143 with TLT, far under the +0.708 that triggered the registry's ban on a correlated second leg. Trend sleeve is flat (state reset 2026-08-03) and the event sleeve holds nothing until 08-21.

reason: Twelve candidates were selected off the surface map across ten asset classes, and eleven died. The event lane was the productive one because today is simultaneously a CPI print and a PPI eve, but its other four expressions all failed: the vehicle translations into IEF and LQD carry no separate mechanism and LQD does not clear its own cost, the spread against SPY adds a leg with negative beta that doubles the bet without adding alpha, and the two commodity and volatility inversions on the same anchor were both beaten by nonsense placebo anchors. The price-state lane came back empty in a coherent way: every one of the four candidates, plus the two the watchlist explicitly owed a check, died on a conditioner that is live today rather than on their headline numbers. Utilities inverted under the SPY-near-high gate that is on, the semis laggard turned out to select tape 35 points more bearish than base rate while today's SMH sits 25% above its 200d, the skew divergence was carried entirely by the not-midterm and not-near-high complement, and the Brazil washout was 71% two episodes. The metals complex was dismissed before its numbers mattered because a live GDX leg runs to 08-17 and the registry rule on correlated second legs applies. One idea is what survived, and padding to three would have meant shipping something already measured as dead.

reason: stale state, plus horizon fragility. Twelve directions across ten cells and seven asset classes, and the market answered the same way in three different accents: the anchor was decoration, the gate did not filter, or the vehicle ate the edge. The two calendar cells the window actually offered, VIX-expiry week and the August pre-opex run, were already swept and dead in the registry, so they were dismissed on their own numbers rather than re-tested. Of what was left, the Jackson Hole legs turned out to be an August month-of-year seasonal wearing an event label (the unconditional Aug 6-16 window pays +1.025% at t=6.90 and thirteen placebo offsets beat the real anchor), the 98th-percentile contango cell is a lagging marker of a short-vol run that has already happened, the macro vacuum is the FOMC exclusion re-labeled, and the fragility dial's rate of change flips sign on its own threshold, its own lookback and its own vintage. One idea reached development and then died to the reference class, which is the honest reason nothing ships: run its rule across 27 sector ETFs and the cross-section is statistically homogeneous at exactly zero.
